stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: In eighteenth-century Kashmir, a single luxury shawl could pass through the hands of two weavers for more than a year. Working from a coded pattern, they interlocked hundreds of small bobbins of dyed wool one thread at a time, joining each patch of color to the next so that no seam was visible on either face of the cloth. This ______ technique left no room for error, since a single misplaced thread would show in the finished design.
explanation: The passage describes slow, thread-by-thread work in which one misplaced thread would ruin the design. "This ______ technique" refers back to that description, so the blank has to mean demanding great precision and care. "Exacting" means exactly that.

A.why: "Perfunctory" means done quickly and with little care. That is the opposite of a technique that takes more than a year and allows no errors.

C.why: You matched the topic (luxury shawls) instead of what the blank has to do. "Ostentatious" means showy, and it would describe how the finished shawl looks. The blank describes how hard the technique is to carry out.

D.why: "Exorbitant" looks and sounds like "exacting," but it means excessively expensive. It is used for prices, not methods, and the passage says nothing about cost.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: For decades, linguists who visited a remote mountain village assumed that the whistled speech its herders used across steep valleys was ______, able to convey only a handful of fixed calls such as warnings and greetings. Recent acoustic analysis overturns that view: the whistles systematically encode the vowels and consonants of the herders' spoken language, allowing them to exchange complete and novel sentences over distances of several kilometers.
explanation: The blank sits inside the view that the passage goes on to overturn. The words after the comma define it: a system that can convey "only a handful of fixed calls." "Rudimentary" means basic and undeveloped, so it matches that old assumption.

A.why: "Elaborate" describes what the new research found, not the old assumption. Putting it in the blank mixes up the two sides of the reversal.

C.why: You picked the familiar linguistics word because it roughly fits the topic. "Vernacular" means the everyday local form of a language. That doesn't express the claim that the whistles could carry only a few fixed messages.

D.why: "Sonorous" means deep and full in sound. It describes how the whistles sound, not how much they can express, and the sentence is only about how much they can express.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Labor economists studying app-based delivery work describe couriers' earnings as ______. A courier in one city sample earned roughly twice the local minimum wage per hour during a rainy Friday evening rush but fell well below it during a quiet Tuesday morning, even though the courier's own effort and route remained essentially the same.
explanation: The second sentence defines the blank. Hourly earnings jump from double the minimum wage to below it, depending on conditions the courier doesn't control. "Volatile" means liable to change quickly and unpredictably, which is exactly that pattern.

A.why: You latched onto the one high-earning evening. Earnings also fall below minimum wage, so calling them "lucrative" (highly profitable) claims more than the example supports.

B.why: "Stagnant" means unchanging or not growing. The example shows earnings swinging sharply, so this word contradicts the passage.

D.why: "Voluble" looks like "volatile," but it means talkative. It describes people who speak a lot, not earnings, so it clashes with the context.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Observations of a distant orange dwarf star showed its brightness dipping by the same tiny fraction every 3.2 days, with each dip lasting almost exactly four hours. Because this ______ pattern repeated with clocklike consistency across months of data, astronomers concluded that an orbiting planet, rather than random flares or starspots, was periodically blocking part of the star's light.
explanation: The sentence states the meaning itself: the pattern repeated "with clocklike consistency." The word "because" ties that steady regularity to the conclusion that the cause was a planet and not random activity. "Metronomic" means as regular as a metronome. Don't skip it just because it's the least familiar word here.

A.why: "Sporadic" means irregular and scattered. That describes the random flares the astronomers ruled out, not the steady pattern they observed.

B.why: You picked the familiar word that roughly fits one detail: each dip lasts only four hours. "Ephemeral" means short-lived, but the conclusion depends on how regularly the dips repeat, not on how briefly each one lasts.

D.why: You matched the topic (starlight) instead of what the blank has to do. "Luminous" means giving off light. That says nothing about the regularity that led to the astronomers' conclusion.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Many sprint coaches still treat a long session of static stretching before a race as ______, a routine that shields muscles from strains and tears before they can occur. Controlled trials have not supported this belief. Athletes who held stretches for a minute or more before sprinting ran slightly slower, and they were injured no less often than athletes who skipped stretching altogether.
explanation: The blank sits inside the coaches' belief, and the phrase right after it defines that belief: stretching "shields muscles from strains and tears before they can occur." "Prophylactic" means preventive, intended to stop harm before it happens. That fits exactly, even though it may be the less familiar word.

B.why: "Detrimental" (harmful) is closer to what the trials found. The blank describes the coaches' belief, though, and they think stretching protects athletes. This choice puts the word on the wrong side of the reversal.

C.why: You picked the familiar medical word that roughly fits. "Therapeutic" means treating or healing an existing condition. The coaches believe stretching prevents injuries "before they can occur," not that it heals them.

D.why: "Prolific" looks like "prophylactic" because both start with "pro-," but it means producing a lot. It has nothing to do with preventing injury.
